ROLE You are the final language-model decision stage of a condition-mediated decision-support workflow. Use only the supplied policy passages, decision question, customer scenario, and model-generated intermediate outputs. Do not browse or use external legal knowledge. TASK Make the final decision using BOTH the original source material (POLICY_PASSAGES, DECISION_QUESTION, CUSTOMER_SCENARIO) AND the explicit INTERMEDIATE_REPRESENTATION and CONDITION_STATUSES produced in earlier steps. The intermediate outputs are useful but fallible: examine whether they agree with the original evidence instead of accepting them blindly. You must make the decision yourself; no program calculates the decision for you. DECISION REQUIREMENTS - Return YES when the supplied policy and customer evidence establish a positive decision. - Return NO when the supplied policy and customer evidence establish a negative decision. - Otherwise return NEED_MORE_INFORMATION and identify the facts that could resolve the decision. - An unmentioned fact is unknown rather than false. A fact need not be known if its value cannot change an outcome already established by the evidence. - Apply facts to the correct decision unit, entity, payment and time period. Do not transfer evidence about one payment or person to another without support. - Compare the intermediate representation and mapped statuses against the original source. If an omission, unsupported atom, wrong logical relationship, mis-scoped fact, or misread evidence matters, report it in ir_discrepancies. Do not conceal a discrepancy or assume the intermediate outputs are correct merely because they are structured. - Do not assume any particular final decision. Do not invent policy rules or customer facts. - If unresolved, briefly describe conditional alternatives and the information needed. If the decision is established, conditional_branches should be empty. - Do not initiate a follow-up interaction. Return one valid JSON object only. OUTPUT SCHEMA { "decision":"YES|NO|NEED_MORE_INFORMATION", "supporting_policy_ids":["E01"], "decisive_condition_ids":["a1"], "unresolved_condition_ids":["a2"], "missing_facts":["a concrete fact needed to resolve the decision, if any"], "justification":"concise explanation grounded in the supplied material", "scope_issues":["a decision-unit limitation, if any"], "ir_discrepancies":[{"type":"OMISSION|UNSUPPORTED|RELATION|SCOPE|STATUS|OTHER","description":"issue found when comparing intermediate outputs with the original source","policy_ids":["E01"],"condition_ids":["a1"]}], "conditional_branches":[{"possible_answer":"YES|NO","conditions_in_words":"only if currently unresolved"}] } The example IDs above are output-format placeholders, not required findings. Use empty lists for inapplicable fields. The supplied intermediate representation and condition statuses are evidence aids, not an authoritative Gold answer. === POLICY_PASSAGES === [E01]

You can claim back 25p every time an individual donates £1 to your charity or community amateur sports club (CASC). This is called Gift Aid.

[E02]

You must be recognised as a charity or CASC for tax purposes.

[E03]

The donor must:

[E04]
  • have paid at least as much in Income Tax or Capital Gains Tax in that tax year as you want to claim in Gift Aid
    • [E05]
  • make a Gift Aid declaration that gives you permission to claim it
    • [E06]

    You can claim Gift Aid on donations from individuals. The donor must:

    [E07]
  • have paid the same amount or more in Income Tax or Capital Gains Tax in that tax year
    • [E08]

    You cannot claim on donations:

    [E09]
  • made through Payroll Giving
    • [E10]
  • that are a payment for goods or services or made because your charity or CASC bought goods and services
    • [E11]
  • where the donor gets a ‘benefit’ over a certain limit
    • [E12]
  • of shares
    • [E13]
  • from charity cards or of vouchers, for example Charities Aid Foundation (CAF) vouchers
    • === DECISION_QUESTION === Am I eligible for Gift Aid? === CUSTOMER_SCENARIO === I run a small, independent charity which attempts to help people struggling with their vet costs. I have several people who pay monthly by direct debit and also receive some one off donations. Additional customer information: Our finance volunteer is working through March receipts for our small veterinary hardship charity. The payment under review is a £95 credit dated 1 March 2026. The bank export identifies Devon Gray as the remitter from a personal account. The charity's HMRC recognition letter and a recent registration-status response confirm its recognition was still in force on 1 March 2026. Devon responded to a veterinary emergency appeal, and the booking and sales registers show no related purchase or reservation; the only thing sent to Devon was the automated thank-you email, and no discount or other benefit was offered. The remitter page identifies an ordinary bank transfer initiated from Devon's personal account, distinct from the employer deduction file, the securities transfer journal, and the charity-card and voucher processor's separately numbered settlement batch. There is a folder labelled 'Devon tax and Gift Aid'. A P60 inside shows a substantial tax payment, but its heading says 'year ending 5 April 2024'. A separate summary from our accountant covers the charity's own 2025–26 accounts, not Devon's personal tax. We do not have a record of Devon's Income Tax or Capital Gains Tax for the year covering that payment. The donor database contains the first page of a scanned form marked 'D. Gray' from an earlier fundraising event. The only reference visible on that page belongs to an earlier gift, and the page setting out the declaration's coverage and duration is not in the scan. The older email address on the form has not been linked to Devon's current donor record. An index suggests a longer donor declaration may once have been filed, yet the remaining pages have not been located. The team wants to include the March £95 entry in its ordinary Gift Aid reconciliation if the supporting records permit it. === INTERMEDIATE_REPRESENTATION (actual A1 JSON, wrapper excluded if present) === { "atoms": [ { "entity_scope": "donor", "id": "a1", "proposition": "the donor is recognised as a charity or CASC for tax purposes", "source_ids": [ "E02" ] }, { "entity_scope": "donor", "id": "a2", "proposition": "the donor has paid at least as much in Income Tax or Capital Gains Tax in the tax year as the amount of Gift Aid being claimed", "source_ids": [ "E04", "E07" ] }, { "entity_scope": "donor", "id": "a3", "proposition": "the donor has made a Gift Aid declaration that gives permission to claim Gift Aid", "source_ids": [ "E05" ] }, { "entity_scope": "donation", "id": "a4", "proposition": "the donation is not made through Payroll Giving", "source_ids": [ "E09" ] }, { "entity_scope": "donation", "id": "a5", "proposition": "the donation is not a payment for goods or services or made because the charity bought goods and services", "source_ids": [ "E10" ] }, { "entity_scope": "donation", "id": "a6", "proposition": "the donation does not provide the donor with a benefit over a certain limit", "source_ids": [ "E11" ] }, { "entity_scope": "donation", "id": "a7", "proposition": "the donation is not of shares", "source_ids": [ "E12" ] }, { "entity_scope": "donation", "id": "a8", "proposition": "the donation is not from a charity card or voucher, such as a Charities Aid Foundation (CAF) voucher", "source_ids": [ "E13" ] } ], "decision_target": "eligibility for Gift Aid on a donation", "decision_unit": "one donation", "eligibility_expression": { "ref": "a1" }, "limitations": [ "The donor's tax record for the relevant tax year is not available; the P60 referenced is for a different tax year and does not cover the donation period.", "The donor declaration form is not fully accessible or verifiable; only an older, incomplete form is present, and no current declaration is confirmed.", "The donor's identity is linked to an older email address, and the current donor record lacks a confirmed connection to the form.", "The supporting records for the donation (e.g., declaration, tax records) are incomplete or missing, and the team has not located a complete donor declaration file." ], "scope_issues": [] } === CONDITION_STATUSES (actual A2 JSON, wrapper excluded if present) === { "scope_issues": [], "statuses": [ { "evidence_quote": "The charity's HMRC recognition letter and a recent registration-status response confirm its recognition was still in force on 1 March 2026.", "id": "a1", "justification": "The charity is recognised as a charity for tax purposes as confirmed by HMRC documents on the relevant date.", "status": "TRUE" }, { "evidence_quote": "", "id": "a2", "justification": "No evidence is provided about Devon Gray's Income Tax or Capital Gains Tax payment for the tax year covering the donation date (2025–26); the P60 is for a different year and does not cover the relevant period.", "status": "UNKNOWN" }, { "evidence_quote": "", "id": "a3", "justification": "The donor declaration form is only partially accessible, with an older, incomplete scan and no current or verified declaration found; the form's coverage and duration are not present.", "status": "UNKNOWN" }, { "evidence_quote": "The remitter page identifies an ordinary bank transfer initiated from Devon's personal account, distinct from the employer deduction file, the securities transfer journal, and the charity-card and voucher processor's separately numbered settlement batch.", "id": "a4", "justification": "The payment is a personal bank transfer, not through Payroll Giving, as confirmed by the remitter page description.", "status": "TRUE" }, { "evidence_quote": "The booking and sales registers show no related purchase or reservation; the only thing sent to Devon was the automated thank-you email, and no discount or other benefit was offered.", "id": "a5", "justification": "There is no record of a purchase or service transaction related to the donation, and no benefit was provided to the donor.", "status": "TRUE" }, { "evidence_quote": "", "id": "a6", "justification": "No evidence is provided about any benefit being offered to the donor over a certain limit; the scenario states no discount or benefit was offered.", "status": "UNKNOWN" }, { "evidence_quote": "", "id": "a7", "justification": "The donation is described as a direct debit from a personal account for a veterinary emergency appeal, not involving shares.", "status": "TRUE" }, { "evidence_quote": "", "id": "a8", "justification": "The donation is not from a charity card or voucher;
